summary: Decision facts span every agent when agent_id is empty (query_bounded drops the agent predicate); the reducer cannot re-filter them. Unreachable today (both callers pin a validated agent). Found independently by security-guardian, architect, cpp-expert, unhappy-path and consistency-auditor. Fixed in c8791b167a: the store returns no facts for an empty agent_id (want_facts), documented, one test section.
No facts test for an unwired plugin set (refuse_unwired). Section added in c8791b167a (pins the observable contract; the lowest-id withheld-row section is what guards the tier clause).

BoundedFacts documentation: `every permitted row` overstated the contract (the facts follow the query's WHERE incl. status/since/until) and the poll's terminal rule (>= 1) differs from the store cap probe's `<> 0`. Reworded and pinned by status -1/99 and filter tests in c8791b167a.

The new constant and BoundedFacts were inserted between the BoundedResponses doc block and its struct (found by architect, cpp-expert, docs-writer, consistency-auditor); the query_bounded paragraph also lost an antecedent. Restored in c8791b167a.

The doubled-output limit (a chunk delivered twice is joined twice) was stated nowhere an operator reads, while the new sentences named 'a late or repeated chunk' as handled; the sentences also overclaimed ('every stored row of the command'), and the `error|` rule only runs after a terminal row. Reworded in rest-api.md, mcp.md, mcp-server.md and the poll header; limit stated in all four in c8791b167a.
Header claimed a per-row agent check as defence in depth; the facts have none (SQL scope only). Header, reduce_rows doc and static_assert comment corrected in c8791b167a.

An `error|` head chunk the cut dropped, with NO terminal row yet, was answered ok+truncated (REST: output_too_large) by the over-cap shortcut. Fixed in c8791b167a: reduce_rows decides kDeviceError when rows_cut and the facts' head is `error|`; PG regression under both over-cap policies and pure cases. Confirmed at Gate 8 across 12 live-kind plugins that no data row begins with `error|`.

The `error|` detail differs between a cut answer (head chunk only) and an uncut one (runs on into the next chunks), and a cut answer whose head is `error|` answers device_error where the uncut device would end as device_failed on its terminal row. Both are the same 502; documented in the poll header, mcp.md and rest-api.md (c8791b167a, 8c234a0331); not unified by design.

Residual ingest-protocol class that the facts cannot see: a redelivered or reordered head chunk (gets a higher id, `error|` no longer first), a failure frame hidden by the Forensics tier (`~unverified`) or refused at the per-agent ingest cap, and a duplicate delivery doubling output (UP-16; agent-side CommandDedupStore replays the original terminal outcome, and whether chunk duplicates reach the store is unverified, hence speculative). Same class as UP-4. Documented in the poll header and the three docs. DERIVED HIGH (I3 wrong result presented as correct, E5 redelivery or a degraded lookup; speculative only for the duplicate-reaches-the-store trigger) and the same class as the owner-ruled UP-4 (document + one issue), but the owner chose 'Fix it in this PR' for G-UP-1 before this residual was scoped: recorded open until the owner rules whether UP-4's disposition extends to it. If it does: deferred-to-issue, one issue for the class, filed on the owner's go (dedupe first).

The G-UP-1 ledger row cross-referenced UP-10 (doubled output) and UP-12 (an error| head): in the earlier ledger UP-10 is the zombie-call finding and UP-12 the gateway sent==1 finding; the doubled-output finding is UP-16 and the head-loss one had no earlier id. Superseded by a pass-2 row for G-UP-1 in this commit.

REST-side statements of the output_too_large rule (rest-api.md Errors line, the OpenAPI operation description and 502 text) lacked the exception for a stored failure or an `error|` head (upgrading.md and the REST fragment already had it). Fixed in c8791b167a (upgrading, fragment) and 8c234a0331 (rest-api.md Errors line, OpenAPI). The ADR-1005 sentence is historical narrative and left alone.

False green: the 'success terminal dropped by the cut' regression passed with the facts off (late rows with output hit the capped short-circuit); the author's own 20-assertion mutation count reconciled only if it contributed zero. The reviewer rated it a policy floor; the derivation gives LOW, recorded SHOULD. Rewritten in c8791b167a with empty-output late rows (facts off gives a timeout); mutation now fails 28 assertions.

The content-bearing head_output subselect had no scope or tier test (the withheld rows held higher ids than the permitted one). Fixed in c8791b167a: withheld rows seeded first (lowest ids), asserting head_output is the permitted row. (The reviewer graded the impact I1 as if the control regressed; the control is correct today, so the missing test is I9.)

Test strength: characters-versus-bytes of left() untested; status/since/until filters with facts untested; seed() ignored the store outcome; the data-head section ran one over-cap policy. Fixed in c8791b167a; the since/until window, the 3-byte clamp case and a UTF-8 skip were tightened in 8c234a0331 after the Gate 8 re-review (QE-1, QE-3, QE-4, cpp-safety F-1). Not changed: the unwired-tier section only pins the observable contract (QE-2); scoped facts (AggregateScope) are untested because no caller passes one (QE-5, revisit at PR C).

The facts CTE was inlined and its aggregate re-ran once per kept row (EXPLAIN loops=64): 4.1 ms against 0.8 ms at 256 rows, 134 ms at 20000 rows. Found by sre and performance with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. Fixed in c8791b167a with AS MATERIALIZED (Gate 8 re-measured: facts run once, 5x faster at the default cap).

At the configured maximum of 65536 rows per agent the facts cost about 110 ms a read (about 21 ms without them); MATERIALIZED does not change it. Non-default setting. Documented in the with_decision_facts comment (c8791b167a); no code change (the alternative subselect shapes measured worse).

The head_output (and failed_detail) top-1 subselects could flip to a responses_pkey walk when the planner estimates about 100 or more rows for the pair: 41 to 95 ms against 0.5 ms, scaling with the table (Gate 8 performance and docs-writer). Fixed in 8c234a0331: `ORDER BY id + 0` (the store's own cap marker uses the same guard); measured by the reviewer.

No signal tells an operator that a device_failed or device_error answer came from the decision facts (the failing row was past the cut), and the response-store read path has no per-read latency histogram or method label on yuzu_server_response_read_degrade_total. The 31-word outcome set is pinned (186 series), so a new label is not added here. Follow-up: a small counter or a sampled log line.
disposition: deferred-to-issue #TBD (observability of facts-decided live answers; response-store read latency by method)
